sponsors: Rep. Alex Burton; coauthor Rep. Matt Commons
status: Died without a committee hearing in House Natural Resources; session adjourned sine die 2026-02-27 with no further action recorded.
key_provisions: Would require data center water regulation through a DNR consumption permit framework before operation.

status: Remained at first reading in House Ways and Means with no hearing recorded; session adjourned sine die 2026-02-27 with no further action.
key_provisions: Would impose labor requirements tied to data center incentives.

sponsors: Rep. Craig Snow; coauthors Reps. Danny Lopez, Harold Slager, Cherrish Pryor; Senate sponsors Sens. Travis Holdman, Scott Baldwin, Ryan Mishler, Linda Rogers, Lonnie Randolph
status: Enacted as Public Law 157; received by the Governor 2026-03-06 and signed 2026-03-12.
key_provisions: Requires certain qualified data center users using transaction award certificates after 2026-06-30 to enter a local agreement contributing up to 1 percent of state gross retail and use tax savings tied to the certificate.

status: Died before receiving a hearing in House Utilities, Energy and Telecommunications; session adjourned sine die 2026-02-27.
key_provisions: Would require an IURC study of data center impacts on utility costs and rates.

status: Died before receiving a hearing in House Utilities, Energy and Telecommunications; session adjourned sine die 2026-02-27.
key_provisions: Water Intensive Facilities: would have authorized Indiana to deny economic incentives to data centers and other large industrial water users unless facilities met specified requirements, including a utility's ability to provide adequate water and the facility paying associated infrastructure costs.

sponsors: Rep. Kendell Culp; coauthors Reps. Jim Pressel and Craig Haggard; Senate sponsors Sens. Eric Koch and Blake Doriot
status: Passed House 2026-02-02 but died without a hearing in Senate Utilities after the land-use preemption language drew public backlash; sponsor confirmed the provision would not advance; session adjourned sine die 2026-02-27.
key_provisions: Proposed land-use preemption for certain developments on agricultural land and data center tax-benefit agreement language. Public and legislative backlash caused the preemption language not to advance.

sponsors: Rep. Jeffrey Thompson (sole author); Senate sponsors Sens. Travis Holdman and Scott Baldwin per the IGA bill detail page
status: Enacted as Public Law 162; received by the Governor 2026-03-06 and signed 2026-03-12.
key_provisions: Requires Indiana Finance Authority, with IEDC, to study data center tax incentives, utility-cost impacts, water-supply impacts, and environmental impacts, with report due to the interim study committee on fiscal policy by 2026-11-01.

status: Died without a hearing in Senate Utilities; session adjourned sine die 2026-02-27.
key_provisions: Energy Utility Matters: would have required large-load customer tariffs to make the large load customer pay all reasonably allocable project costs regardless of eventual usage, capped IURC-approved rate increases relative to national electricity price growth, restricted utility cost recovery for lobbying/political/charitable spending, and directed a 2026 interim study of utility cost trackers.

status: Died without a hearing in Senate Utilities; session adjourned sine die 2026-02-27 with no further action recorded.
key_provisions: Would limit electric rate increases attributable to data centers or similar large-load facilities under specified conditions.

sponsors: Sen. J.D. Ford; second author Sen. Spencer Deery
status: Died without a hearing in Senate Utilities; session adjourned sine die 2026-02-27 with no further action recorded.
key_provisions: Would create an IURC working group on projected data center electricity demand and require quarterly electricity-use reporting by data center operators.
